title: Hot Cocoa Mix

drivers.name: Price increase (3.4%)
drivers.evidence: Price rose to $5.20 from $5.03. Recent weeks at same price show no uplift (median 32 vs baseline 30.5). Price sensitivity is evident in past promotions (e.g., 2026-06-15: 20% off, only 3 units).

drivers.name: Competitor store opening
drivers.evidence: Planner note: new competitor across the street. No direct data, but plausible demand diversion. Risk is non-trivial and not offset by any promotional or event driver.

drivers.name: Thanksgiving (event week)
drivers.evidence: Historical median x1.12, but noise-adjusted estimate is x1.0. Only 3 past occurrences, one outlier (2023: 74 units). Not enough evidence to justify lift.

adjustment.analysis: The baseline median is 30.5. Thanksgiving (event week) has a historical median lift of x1.12 vs baseline, but the noise-adjusted estimate is x1.0 due to limited, inconsistent evidence (only 3 past occurrences, one outlier). The price increase to $5.20 (+3.4%) is above regular price ($5.03), and recent weeks show no promotion lift at this price, suggesting a price-sensitive product. A competitor opening across the street introduces demand loss risk, though no direct evidence. The classical uplift model suggests no change, but judgment overrides this: price increase and new competitor likely suppress demand. No promotion or seasonal ramp is active. The median is adjusted down to reflect these headwinds. Spreads widen slightly due to uncertainty.

brief:
PRODUCT: Hot Cocoa Mix | category Grocery | Store #12 (Austin, TX)
TARGET WEEK: 2026-11-23 to 2026-11-29 (7 weeks after the last week with sales data)

KNOWN PLAN FOR THE TARGET WEEK:
  events: Holiday: Thanksgiving (Thu)
  shelf price: 5.20 (+3.4% vs regular price 5.03)
  planner notes: A competitor opens a store across the street this week

STATISTICAL BASELINE (exponential smoothing of recent sales; it ignores events, promotions and prices):
  median 30.5 | 5%-95%: 0.0 - 50.3 | 10%-90%: 5.1 - 49.8

In the evidence below, 'vs baseline' = actual units / what this same baseline predicted for that week.
It is the multiplier that would have been right, so it maps directly onto median_multiplier.
This product's ordinary weeks already swing about +/-77% around the baseline, so a past effect smaller than that, seen only a few times, is mostly noise. The
'noise-adjusted estimate' is the effect shrunk toward x1.0 for that noise and the number of sightings.
